question: Which festival is celebrated on the last day of the Hindu month of Shravan to mark the end of the monsoon season in the western coastal areas of India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Narali Purnima**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narali Purnima is the festival celebrated** on the full moon day of the Hindu month of Shravan to mark the end of the monsoon season in the western coastal areas of India.
 
• It is **also known as the Coconut Festival.** 
 
• Narali Purnima **is celebrated by the Hindu fishing communities in Maharashtra, India, especially around Mumbai **and the Konkan coast. 
 
• The** festival marks the end of the monsoon season when fishermen can safely resume fishing. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kojagiri Purnima**

 
 
• **​**Kojagiri Purnima **is a Hindu festival that takes place on the full moon day of the Ashwin month**.
 
• It is **also known as Sharad Purnim**a. 
 
• **The festival celebrates the full moon and the end of the monsoon season. **
 
• **It is dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity. ​**
 
 
 
• **Samba Dashami** 
 
 
• Samba Dashami **is a festival unique to the state of Odisha,** India.
 
• It is **celebrated on the 10th day of the Shukla Paksha of Pausha Māsa or waxing phase of moon in the month of Pausha (December – January) as per traditional Odia calendar.**
 
• This festival is especially celebrated in the eastern part of Odisha.
 
 
 
• Guru Purnima
 
 
• Guru Purnima is a significant Hindu festival celebrated in honor of the spiritual gurus, mentors, and teachers in one's life. 
 
• The festival falls on the full moon day or Purnima of the Hindu month of Ashadha (June-July in the Gregorian calendar). 
 
• The word 'Guru' is derived from the Sanskrit language and means 'teacher' or 'guide,' while 'Purnima' means 'full moon day'. 
 
• It is believed that Guru Purnima is the day when the great sage Vyasa, who is considered the Adi Guru or the first Guru in Hinduism, was born.
 
• Therefore, the day is also known as Vyasa Purnima.
